It can happen, but it’s not fair to assume delivery workers generally lack attention to detail based on one bad experience. Delivery jobs often involve tight schedules, heavy workloads, unfamiliar addresses, app or routing issues, and pressure to complete many stops quickly—all of which can lead to mistakes.

Some workers are very careful and reliable; others may be rushed, inexperienced, distracted, or simply having an off day. If the errors caused a real problem, your friend could give specific, factual feedback to the delivery company so it can be addressed without making broad assumptions about the worker or the profession.

That sounds genuinely frustrating, especially if it has happened repeatedly. A pattern in your friend’s area may point to local factors—confusing house numbers, unclear unit labels, inaccurate map pins, similar-looking homes, poorly lit addresses, or a route/service that pressures drivers to move too quickly.

- Use a distinctive landmark in instructions if allowed.
- Request photo confirmation or a signature for important items.
- Report repeated misdeliveries with dates, photos, and tracking numbers; the carrier may be able to flag the address or speak with the local route manager.

Your friend’s experience is valid evidence that something needs fixing, even if it doesn’t establish that all delivery workers lack attention to detail.
